A few days ago, @UNICEF published a report determining that acute malnutrition rates in Gaza are as low as 0.2%–0.8%. The report notes that this rate reflects greater stability than in many other countries in the region. These findings align with the humanitarian report that we in COGAT published several weeks ago, which determined that the volume of food entering the Gaza Strip during the ceasefire significantly exceeded humanitarian needs. Since the start of the ceasefire, over 2 million tons of food have entered Gaza. This massive influx has led to: 📉 A sharp drop in food prices. 🥗 Greater dietary diversity in local markets. 🍞 Dozens of active bakeries and community kitchens. COGAT’s coordination efforts, in cooperation with the international community, have maintained a stable food situation in Gaza. The data speaks for itself. Backed by hard facts, it is clear that the steady flow of aid is meeting and exceeding humanitarian needs, securing long-term stability on the ground. Read COGAT’s full report here: https://bit.ly/4p8iCOp

The General Directorate of Coasts and Borders Security concluded the first Pistol Shooting Championship for Officers, featuring individual and team competitions. The three-day championship was attended by 33 officers of various ranks representing the directorate’s departments and sections. The championship aimed to enhance field readiness, develop shooting skills, and foster a spirit of positive competition among officers, contributing to the development of their professional capabilities and the advancement of security performance. At the conclusion of the championship, Colonel (Navy) Hassan Ahmed Al-Sulaiti, Director General of Coasts and Borders Security, crowned the winners in the presence of several department directors and section heads. #MOIQatar
